chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him)

that a man visited him and said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the proof for the origination of the world? He said: You were non-existent, then you came into existence. And you know that you did not bring yourself into existence, nor did one like you bring you into existence.

key_terms.الدليل: Proof, evidence — a rational argument establishing a doctrinal point
key_terms.حدث العالم: Origination of the world (huduth al-alam) — the theological position that the world has a beginning in time, not eternal

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic proof that the world was created?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a succinct cosmological argument for the creation of the universe. When asked for proof that the world is originated, he points to the questioner's own existence as evidence: you once did not exist, then you came to be. Since you neither created yourself nor could any contingent being like you have created you, there must be a transcendent Creator. This argument from contingency was a well-known theological proof in Islamic kalam.
